evidence.point: The client operates 3 counters, which is the primary feature contributing to the risk score according to SHAP analysis [SNAPSHOT].
The client has a long tenure of 31.15 years, which is identified as the second most significant factor in the risk model [SNAPSHOT].
Consumption data shows high skewness (3.4228) and kurtosis (13.1063), placing the client in the 95.5th and 94.7th percentiles respectively, suggesting irregular usage patterns [SNAPSHOT].

The ratio of consumption in the last two years compared to the lifetime average is 1.7108, which is in the 94.3rd percentile, indicating a significant recent change in consumption behavior [SNAPSHOT].
The account record indicates the presence of missing months, which may impact the accuracy of consumption tracking [SNAPSHOT].
